maya: Heads-up — after last night's deploy (canary 3.4.2) we're seeing a +~80ms jump in 99th tail latency for small-response hosted inference. Repro is pretty stable on the canary. Traced to host-side tokenization + stream pacing overheads, not GPU. Sample profiler below.

devon: Can you paste the logs / flame summary? cc @eli

maya: Quick log snippets: parse_time jumped from ~2.1ms -> ~12.4ms, stream_chunk_send from 0.6ms -> 10.8ms. Host proxy CPU in top shows lots of time in tokenize_utf8 and grpc_writev. Flame breakdown pasted: 

```
tokenize_utf8        52.3%   12.4ms
grpc_writev          18.7%    4.4ms
accept_batch         14.1%    3.3ms
kv_cache_lookup       5.2%    1.2ms
other_syscalls        9.7%    2.3ms
```

devon: That smells like tokenizer lock contention + a higher # of tiny batches. Did we change batching heuristics in the last release? Maybe adaptive small-batcher defaults flipped.

eli: We did tweak adaptive_batcher last week to lower p50 latency by forcing smaller caps when concurrency is low. That change increases the number of batches for high-concurrency small-seq workloads, which raises syscall + stream overhead. Also saw a kernel-selection fallback path that does synchronous probes for int8 kernels for small seqs — that probe can cause a short stall on first few requests.

sophia: Do we have a clear repro script? If average seq len is tiny and RPS is high, prefix caching (hot shard) could help reduce tokenization/kv lookup overhead. We can flip prefix_kv_hot_shard for the canary and see.

maya: I have a repro harness (local + canary): rps=1200, avg_tokens=8, tail_tokens=64. Repro command: `./repro.sh --rps 1200 --seq_avg 8 --seq_tail 64` — run that against canary and you'll see the spikes. I'll enable prefix_kv for tonight and collect another profile.

devon: Short-term mitigation ideas:
- bump batching delay ms for small sequences to ~6ms (fewer syscalls)
- disable adaptive_small_batcher flag on canary
- offload UTF8 tokenization to a small threadpool or use vectorized byte-level tokenizer to reduce per-request syscall cost

eli: Long-term: move kernel probe off the hot path. Right now runtime probes int4/int8 kernels on first use for small seqs and does it synchronously; move that to an async probe + cache kernel choices per model-version. That should remove the per-request jitter when new kernel path is selected.

sophia: I'll apply a canary config set: `adaptive_small_batcher=false`, `batching_delay_ms=6`, `prefix_kv_hot_shard=true` and add a temporary per-route dashboard for trace/span tail. I'll also schedule a longer canary run (2h) and attach the repro harness to it.

runtime-bot: deploy-bot: Canary config updated for service "hosted-runtime" — change set cs_789 started. Link: https://ci.redwood/dev/changes/cs_789 :rocket:

maya: After rolling those flags to canary we saw ~60ms drop in 99th over a 15m window. Still seeing infrequent spikes when the batcher receives a burst of longer tails. Next steps: eli -> async kernel probe; devon -> tokenizer offload PR; sophia -> longer canary and perf dashboard + eval with skewed token lengths.

devon: Assigning work: devon -> tokenizer offload draft (PR #4567), eli -> kernel probe async (PR #4568), sophia -> canary dashboard & perf test (ticket PERF-312).

maya: I'll leave the repro running overnight and collect flame profiles + trace samples. If anything else shows up I'll post here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
